subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR’s native @microsoft/mxc-sdk dependency graph and argv-carried base64 config transport for an official prerelease MXC sandbox plugin?
rationale: The code defect has a narrow fix, but accepting a native sandbox SDK, node-pty install script, packaged executor binaries, and config-on-argv transport is a security/product boundary choice that automation cannot make.

options.title: Approve after fail-closed policy fix
options.body: Fix the missing-policy-file behavior, then allow the exact-head dependency graph and document the preview SDK transport as accepted prerelease risk.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until @microsoft/mxc-sdk offers a non-argv config transport or stronger sandbox config handling.

options.title: Keep MXC external only
options.body: Decline first-party official packaging for now and ask the contributor to maintain the MXC backend outside this repository through ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Approve after fail-closed policy fix
recommendation.body: Fix the missing-policy-file behavior, then allow the exact-head dependency graph and document the preview SDK transport as accepted prerelease risk.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest recent review trail on the MXC/OpenShell sandbox contract and the remaining security-boundary question.
